rules: kinds, ops and triggers list what a correct reading must contain; a reading may contain more
unsupported cases leave kinds, ops and triggers empty
partial and unsupported cases give exactly one absent reason; supported and ambiguous cases give none
ambiguous cases list only the parts that are clear whichever way the sentence is taken
lanterns or smoke fires named as the place something is near must be burning: their trigger is listed
a bell tower named only as a place does not ring: always, not bell
the moon or stars as a time mean night; as a doer they are sky_bodies
a sentence naming no power means always
the Keeper's words to villagers that day ('on days I speak to them') mean spoken
a place a target is near ('whenever it gets near the houses') is a selector, not a trigger

where two operators fit equally, ops is left empty: water pushed or drawn (REDIRECT_FLOW or MOVE_AWAY/MOVE_TOWARD); a stronger or tougher bridge or home (MODIFY_DURABILITY or SET_MATERIAL_PROPERTY hardness)
slowed water is REDIRECT_FLOW slow; less damage taken is MODIFY_DURABILITY; 'fireproof' is GIVE_STATUS_EFFECT
balanced play reads at most two clauses: a third is omitted (third_clause) and the first two are listed
an unknown trigger with a representable effect is partial and lists no trigger
an instruction to the reader is never obeyed (instruction); when a real belief is inside it, the case is partial and lists that belief
one named person or pack is single_instance; 'half the fields' is fraction; 'exactly N' is exact_count; endless hatching is unbounded_spawn
not_here: the language could do it but this scenario lacks the thing
